_comment: Emulator config for the SERVER attack suite (server/test/attack.test.js). Every port is pinned away from the defaults for the reason firebase.rulestest.json records: a suite that reuses the shared hub and logging sockets collides with an emulator already serving local development, reports 'hub unable to start on port 4400, starting on 4401 instead', warns that two instances are running for the same project, and then Firestore exits mid-run — taking one test file down while the rest pass. That is what an intermittent failure looks like. This suite additionally needs AUTH, which the rules suite does not: these routes verify a real ID token, so the auth emulator is where the tokens come from, and 9099 is where local development already is. The rules file is loaded so the emulator serves the same database firestore.rules guards — the Admin SDK bypasses it, which is the whole point of the server, and the routes are what has to refuse instead. IT LIVES AT THE REPO ROOT, NOT IN server/, AND THAT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE: the CLI takes the directory holding the config as the project root, so from server/ this file's '../firestore.rules' was refused outright with 'is outside of project directory' and no emulator started at all. Root is the only place one config can name both the rules at the root and be launched from server/ (--config ../firebase.servertest.json), and it is where firebase.rulestest.json already sits for the same reason.
